A new name at the backend of the year was Nigel Bevan, one of the country's leading Javelin throwers, who became a member on 17 August and five days after that set new club figures for a Senior and Junior with 71.66 representing Southern Counties in Norway.
Nigel Bevan

Individual wins were recorded by Ernie Obeng 100m, Marcus Adam 200m, Stu Paton 1500m, Mike Hayes 3000 S/C, Femi Abejide Triple Jump and Nigel Bevan, Javelin Throw and the 4x400m Relay Team of Cuff, Busk, Maynard and Paton.
Welcome to new members to our teams, Ossie Cham, Femi Abejide, Nigel Bevan and Lennie Paul. You are always assured of a great welcome to our Track and Field team.
Nigel Bevan was 2nd in the Javelin with a 70.42m throw and Jimmy Summers had a 54.58m Hammer Throw. Jimmy also teamed up with Bob Bridges to get valuable points in the Pole Vault.
In the field new member Femi Abejedi finished 2nd in the triple jump with 15.86, whilst a pb throw of 74.60m in the javelin for Nigel Bevan was only enough for 4th.

Meanwhile, Nigel Bevan, who had been prostrated most of the afternoon by a trapped nerve in his back, had been advised by the Blackheath physio. not to compete.
Ray Chambers and Simon Shirley gained valuable points in the javelin, Nigel Bevan's absence due to a sudden knee operation - it was doubtful if he would throw again during the season.
Our best performance came from Nigel Bevan who justified his selection with a season's best of 77.80m. This could only suffice for 4th spot and was shades of Auckland.
The throws were progressing nicely with Abi winning the discus and finishing fourth in the shot while Nigel Bevan just missed second in the javelin by 36cm.
Nigel Bevan, back to full training after his operation, was out of sorts, grumbling to himself until he finally got it together to snatch second in the 'A' javelin.
